classification.difficultyReason: Explain the four combinations of leading-coefficient sign and degree parity.

content.prompt: Consider the behaviour of a polynomial for large positive and large negative numbers. Explain how this depends on whether the leading coefficient $a_n$ is positive or negative, and whether $n$ is even or odd.

answer.short:
If $n$ is even, both ends rise when $a_n>0$ and both ends fall when $a_n<0$. If $n$ is odd, the left end falls and the right end rises when $a_n>0$; the left end rises and the right end falls when $a_n<0$.

For large $|x|$, the leading term $a_nx^n$ determines the behaviour.
answer.worked:
For large $|x|$, the leading term $a_nx^n$ dominates the lower-degree terms. An even power is positive for both positive and negative $x$; an odd power has the same sign as $x$.

• If $a_n>0$ and $n$ is even, $P(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$ and as $x\to+\infty$.

• If $a_n>0$ and $n$ is odd, $P(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$, and $P(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to+\infty$.

• If $a_n<0$ and $n$ is even, $P(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$ and as $x\to+\infty$.

• If $a_n<0$ and $n$ is odd, $P(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$, and $P(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to+\infty$.
